mia.dev: hitting a pretty gnarly hang in the Python async SDK when an auth retry happens. client stops returning and new requests queue up.
jonathan: ugh, that sounds like connection reuse after a 401/403 path. any logs?
mia.dev: short repro below, will paste logs. happening on uvloop + httpx async client in our app.
mia.dev: repro steps:
```
# start app
python examples/async_repro.py --concurrency 50
# then trigger an auth rotation that causes 401s for ~10s
```
mia.dev: logs show repeated "reused closed transport" warnings then tasks pending forever. snippet: 
```
ERROR httpx._exceptions.ConnectionNotAvailable: Connection pool is full, no available connections.
WARNING connection: attempted reuse of closed transport (fd 42)
Task exception: asyncio.exceptions.TimeoutError
```
alex: can you paste the client config? pool settings, keepalive, max_connections, etc.
mia.dev: default SDK config in our code, we didn't override keepalive or max_lifetime. using AsyncRedwoodClient() context manager.
priya: two things to investigate: 1) pool doesn't evict connections that errored during auth retry, 2) __aenter__/__aexit__ typing for AsyncRedwoodClient is wrong which masks incorrect usage in user code (mypy silence).
jonathan: interesting — if a retry consumes the underlying transport exception path, the connection could be marked usable and re-enqueued. then subsequent requests pick it up and hang.
sam: workaround for now: explicitly set a short max_connection_lifetime and smaller pool_limit, or call client.close() in the auth-refresh path. e.g.
```
async with AsyncRedwoodClient(..., pool_limit=20, connection_max_lifetime=30) as client:
    ...
# or
await client.aclose()
```
mia.dev: tried connection_max_lifetime=30 and it helped reduce occurrence but didn't eliminate. calling aclose() on token refresh seems to fix reliably.
priya: I'm working on a typing/contract PR to make the async client context manager type-safe so mypy warns when clients are stored globally and not used inside context. will also add an explicit `is_alive()` check in the pool.
alex: could we add a fast path on retry errors to mark connection as bad and not reuse? that avoids global close.
jonathan: yes, mark transport as CLOSED on ConnectionResetError / 401 during request and drop it from pool. add a countermeasure for in-flight KV cache cleanup too.
mia.dev: attaching minimal log + stack trace here (paste):
```
Task: <Task pending name='Task-12' coro=<Request._async_run() running at ...>
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/asyncio/tasks.py", line 500, in wait
  await fut
ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
... then pool puts connection back
```
infra-bot: test run queued: devex/async-connpool-ci #482.
sam: I'll open an issue and a small repro in the SDK repo with these logs and suggested workaround steps. tagging @alex for runtime follow-up and @priya for typing PR.
priya: also proposing a small API addition: Client.ensure_connection_health() and a `on_error_drop=True` default for auth-related errors. makes retry path explicit.
alex: sounds good. priority: bugfix for connection eviction on auth error, small typing PR, and a short doc note for token rotation patterns.
mia.dev: thanks — opened issue #2389 and pushed repro script to gist: https://gist.github.com/mia/async-repro. will try the aclose() workaround in prod next deploy and report back. :thumbsup:
